readings: Overlapping detection: the last 1 of a 1101 match can also be the first 1 of the next match, so 1101101 contains two 1101 sequences.
Non-overlapping detection: after a 1101 match, the FSM resets its search progress and requires four entirely new bits before another match.

Outputs are Moore (combinational from state) and change only after the clock edge that updates the state; e.g., shift_ena is high the cycle after the fourth pattern bit is sampled, and done is high the cycle after done_counting is sampled high.

Outputs are Mealy or registered with one-cycle delay; e.g., shift_ena could be high in the same cycle the fourth pattern bit is sampled, and done could be high in the same cycle done_counting is high.
The FSM must enter the done state and assert done for at least one cycle before checking ack; if ack is already high when done_counting is high, done still pulses one cycle.
If ack is already high when done_counting is high, the FSM can transition directly to search without entering the done state, so done may never be asserted.
The pattern is matched in time order: the first incoming bit is the leftmost 1, then a 1, then a 0, then a 1.
The pattern is matched as a binary value 1101 with the first incoming bit being the LSB, i.e., the time-order sequence is 1-0-1-1.
